question: im transferring from bergen community college with an associates in liberal arts, do i still have to do all the gen eds at ramapo or does the AA cover them?
answer:
No. Ramapo says students with an A.A. or A.S. from a New Jersey community college are waived from General Education Requirements after submitting a final official transcript with the conferred degree [6, 10]. Bergen is not named individually, but the pages apply to New Jersey community colleges [5, 6]. An A.A. is described as fully transferable as the first two years of a bachelor’s degree at New Jersey four-year institutions [14]. Ramapo’s catalog also says A.A. or A.S. students from a New Jersey community college should refer to its transfer-credit policy for more information [12].

Submit a final official transcript showing the conferred degree to receive the waiver [10]. Ramapo says A.A. or A.S. holders from a New Jersey community college have completed all general education requirements and do not need placement tests [9].

Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7300 [6, 10].

Sources: [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/admitted-students/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [12](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#waiver-of-general-education-requirements1) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#transferring-academic-credit1)

question: how many credits do i need total to graduate from ramapo and how many of those have to be taken at ramapo itself
answer:
For an undergraduate degree, the published pages say you need at least 128 credits overall; some degree programs may require more. [4][5][6][8]

The pages differ on how many credits must be completed at Ramapo: the Registrar FAQ says a minimum of 32 credits at Ramapo [4], the Registrar’s graduation page says a minimum of 48 [5][6], and the Catalog says a minimum of 32 [7][8]. The Catalog also says the final 32 credits must be completed in residence; its residency page allows those credits at Ramapo or in a Ramapo College-approved study abroad program or experience. [7][8]

For clarification, contact the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7695, D-224. [4][5][6]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#undergraduate-residency-requirement1) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#graduation-requirements)

question: does ramapo have a nursing program for transfer students or is it only freshmen
answer:
Ramapo’s nursing options are not limited to freshmen. The Accelerated BSN is for applicants with a non-nursing bachelor’s degree or at least 60 credits from a regionally accredited institution [1]. Accelerated BSN applicants must have a 3.0 cumulative GPA or above; transfer students are strongly recommended to have at least a 2.5 cumulative GPA [7]. Its requirements and application instructions are here: https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-requirements/ and https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-instructions/ [5].
There is also an RN-to-BSN track for registered nurses with an associate’s degree or nursing diploma; students transfer credits from their initial nursing program [3]. The generic BSN track is another option, but its page describes the first two years as general education and science requirements [2].
For transfer admission questions, contact Admissions at admissions@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7300 [5][7].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURA) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/)

question: how many credits is the minor in data science and which courses are in it

question: Do the transfer seminar or first year seminar requirements apply to me if I'm coming in as a junior?
answer:
The pages don’t say whether a separate “Transfer Seminar” is required. For that, contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207 [2].

First-Year Seminar is described as designed for first-time, full-time, first-year students [1], and is a general education requirement for first-year students to be taken in the fall of their first year [2]. Transfer students may transfer in or be waived from some or all General Education requirements under the stated policies [3]. Specifically, transfers without an A.A. or A.S. degree from a New Jersey community college who have at least 48 credits from an accredited institution are waived from First Year Seminar; during academic advisement, students are advised about applicable waivers and remaining requirements [4]. Being a junior alone doesn’t establish whether that waiver applies.

For transfer-waiver guidance, contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330 [3].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/INTD101) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#waiver-of-general-education-requirements1)

question: im a transfer starting the computer science major in the fall with my math done, whats the recommended order of the cs courses for the next 2 years
answer:
For the Computer Science BS (Bachelor of Science), the Fall 2026 recommended graduation plan applies to students admitted to the major in 2026–2027; it is a four-year plan, not a transfer-specific sequence. [1]

Following its first two years, the CS courses are:
1. First-year fall: CMPS 147 Computer Science I.
2. First-year spring: CMPS 148 Computer Science II, then CMPS 220 Assembly Language Programming.
3. Second-year fall: CMPS 231 Data Structures.
4. Second-year spring: CMPS 311 Operating Systems and a CMPS elective. [1]

The plan also places MATH 237 or MATH 205 in second-year fall; it does not say how to adjust the sequence for math already completed or transfer credit. Plan: https://www.ramapo.edu/recommended-graduation-plan-2026/tas/computer-science/ [1]

Other published levels: Computer Science 4+1, Computer Science MS, Computer Science Minor, Mathematics Minor. [1]

I don’t have verified information about a transfer-adjusted sequence for your completed math. The Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) may help: success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207.

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-CMPS)

question: does a 3 credit course from community college count the same as a ramapo 4 credit course toward a major requirement?
answer:
Not necessarily as the same major requirement. Ramapo says a 3-credit class earns 3 credits; remaining credits can be packaged together to make a complete class. The same total number of credits is needed to complete a Ramapo degree. [5][6] This does not confirm that a particular community-college course satisfies a specific major requirement. Ramapo says outside credits may apply if they meet the criteria for their type of transfer credit. [11]

For New Jersey county-college course equivalencies, Ramapo directs students to www.NJTransfer.org. [8] The Registrar advises reviewing the number of classes and credits with your adviser. [15]

For confirmation of your course’s equivalency, contact Admissions at admissions@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7300. [5][8] Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695. [15]
